back: Diseases caused by uncontrolled mitosis of cells with mutated cell-cycle genes; malignant tumours invade and spread.
Benign: slow, encapsulated, does not spread. Malignant: invades tissue, metastasises via blood or lymph.
Proto-oncogene: normal gene promoting division. Oncogene: mutated, permanently active form.
Gene whose protein stops division or triggers apoptosis when DNA is damaged (e.g. p53); loss of function allows cancer.
Spread of cancer cells from a primary tumour through blood or lymph to form secondary tumours.
Chemicals (tobacco tar, aflatoxins), ionising radiation, UV radiation, some viruses (HPV, hepatitis B).

front: Why does chemotherapy cause side effects?
back: It targets dividing cells, so hair follicles, gut lining and bone marrow are also affected.

front: Why does cancer risk rise with age?
back: Several mutations must accumulate in one cell line over time.
Detect precancerous or early changes before symptoms, when treatment is most successful.
